issue.title: [IE9] Including router produces error

body: So is the Angular 2 team calling this a bug or are they not supporting a shim for IE9?  I have to support IE9 and this affects my routing decisions.

issue.title: IE9 - pushState
issue.body:
This is a Bug
Browser : Internet Explorer 9
Operating System : Windows 7
Angular : 2 beta 13

After adding `shims_for_IE.js` from angular2 repository for missing `requestAnimationFrame`, now I am facing issue with `pushState`.

Because of this, I am not able to move to other pages and the URL is not updating with the hash.

![ie9-pushstate](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/897339/14195792/58e3d06a-f772-11e5-973a-1b61f6d4ff24.png)

body:
As a workaround you could just provider a custom `LocationStrategy` (for example extend the `PathLocationStrategy` or `HashLocationStrategy` and override the behavior you want have changed then provide it like

``` ts
bootstrap(AppComponent, [ROUTER_PROVIDERS, provide(LocationStrategy, {useClass: MyLocationStrategy})
```

then you don't have to modify `angular2.dev.js`

- https://github.com/angular/angular/tree/master/modules/angular2/src/router/location 
  You need to override the code that offeneds IE9. 
  Sorry, I don't plan to spend time for IE9 (I'm not a member of the Angular team)

body:
Before @sasidhar PR is merged, you can override Angular2's https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/modules/angular2/src/router/location/browser_platform_location.ts that is suspected of having the problem as making your own 'browser_platform_location.ts'.

Just make a clone of this https://github.com/sasidhar/angular/blob/6af02a0df54a8744003e4075b1bd077be976ea3f/modules/angular2/src/router/location/browser_platform_location.ts and change the class name to MyBrowserPlatformLocation

Lastly do DEPENDENCY INJECTION like bootstrap(AppComponent, [ROUTER_PROVIDERS, provide(PlatformLocation, {useClass: MyBrowserPlatformLocation})

It is a temporary solution but it worked to me.

issue.title: this.router.navigate(...) doesn't work in IE9
issue.body:
**Steps to reproduce and a minimal demo of the problem**

Open this plnkr in IE9.

http://plnkr.co/edit/IJ6tcuVOb5npbElvQzbq?p=preview

`this.router.navigate(...);` in home.component.ts does nothing at all when you click the button. It should tack on a #/test route to the URL and show the other component. 

_What steps should we try in your demo to see the problem?_

Using IE9, click the only button on the screen to take you to the Test view. You'll notice nothing shows up in the console and the routing doesn't happen. The page content doesn't change and the URL doesn't update to show the new route. In Chrome or later versions of IE it will successfully route to the new view.

**Expected/desired behavior**

Routing should update URL and page contents in IE9.

**Other information**

There is zero information in the console. No indication at all for a failure.
